transcript.content: Hi, I'm Dr. Lee. It's nice to meet you. Could you start by telling me what brings you in to see me today?

Yeah, hi, Doctor. So… I guess what finally got me to come in is that I’m having a really hard time keeping my attention on things I absolutely need to be paying attention to. Like at work, I’m a construction manager, and I’ll be in a safety briefing or reviewing a plan, and I’ll start out telling myself, “Okay, focus, this is important, don’t miss anything.” And I really do try.

But then within a few minutes, my head is already somewhere else — like thinking about some issue on another part of the job, or a call I need to make, or three other problems that are all kind of bouncing around at once. And then I realize I’ve missed something that was just said or something on the plan that I know I should have caught. It’s frustrating because these aren’t little throwaway things, you know? They matter. And I’m not trying to be careless. I’ll be sitting right there, looking like I’m listening, but my mind just drifts off before I even notice it happened.

Thinking back, did you notice this kind of difficulty focusing and easily getting distracted back when you were a child or teenager, or is this something that's really only become a problem more recently, say in the last several months to a year?

No, this definitely isn’t just the last year or something. I mean, it’s gotten more serious now because the stakes at work are higher, but when I think back, this was there when I was a kid too.

Even in elementary school, teachers were already telling my parents about it. I remember them saying I couldn’t stay in my seat, or I’d be talking when I wasn’t supposed to, blurting things out before it was my turn. And homework was a whole thing — I’d lose it, forget where I put it, or bring home the wrong stuff. My parents would get frustrated because it looked like I just didn’t care, but I did… I just couldn’t seem to keep track of things the way other kids did.

And with directions, I’d rush right into something before I really understood what the teacher had said. Like I’d hear the first part and just go, and then realize halfway through I’d missed some important piece of it. So yeah, looking back, it was showing up pretty early. It’s not new.
These days, as an adult, do you still notice things like feeling restless or fidgety, having trouble sitting still, interrupting others, or acting impulsively before thinking things through?

Yeah, the sitting still part is definitely still there. Meetings are probably the easiest example. If everybody else can sit through the whole thing, I’m usually the guy who’s standing up at some point, walking over to get coffee, stepping outside “to check on something,” or making some excuse to move around.

And sometimes there really is something to check, but if I’m being honest, a lot of times it’s just that I feel like I can’t stay planted in the chair anymore. I’ll start feeling kind of wound up, like I need to shift or get up, and then I’m looking for a reason that makes it seem normal. I don’t always want people noticing it, especially because I’m supposed to be the one managing things, but yeah… sitting through a whole meeting like everyone else is hard for me.
